subject: Question about manually setting initial values

messages.author: 7fd65ccbd9861e6b
messages.subject: Question about manually setting initial values
parts:
Hi all-

I'm working with the developer of the Julia interface for Stan on validating the manual initialization of parameter values. When I print out the parameters to the runlog (see below), only one of the parameters is equal to the values I set manually. This strikes me as odd. I expected the first set of parameters to be the initial values I set.  Is it possible that the printing is suppressed for the initial parameters?

Thanks,

Chris 

model {
  omega ~ gamma(2,3);
  kappa ~ beta(7,3);
  theta ~ beta(A,B);
  print("omega");
  print(omega);
  print("kappa");
  print(kappa);
  print("theta[1]");
  print(theta[1]);
  print("theta[2]");
  print(theta[2]);
  for (obs in 1:Nobs){
    y[obs] ~ bernoulli(theta[SubjIdx[obs]]);
  }
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Question about manually setting initial values
parts:
On Thursday, April 27, 2017 at 2:51:41 PM UTC-4, Christopher Fisher wrote:
I'm working with the developer of the Julia interface for Stan on validating the manual initialization of parameter values. When I print out the parameters to the runlog (see below), only one of the parameters is equal to the values I set manually. This strikes me as odd. I expected the first set of parameters to be the initial values I set.  Is it possible that the printing is suppressed for the initial parameters?

The initial parameters you pass from Julia (or whatever interface) start going through the leapfrog process before the first execution of the print statements in the model block. In RStan, we basically had to save the initial values before NUTS starts in order to preserve them in the stanfit object at the end.

Ben
